title: Chapter 25: Boss Level 5: The Data Report Generator
video_title: Python Chapter 25: Boss Level 5, The Data Report Generator
summary: Every evening the Corner Cafe till saves a messy CSV file. Follow Asha as she builds a report generator that reads every file, skips and counts bad rows, takes its settings from JSON and gives one clear message instead of a crash. An AI assistant helps at all six stages. Her real files and her tests catch its confident mistakes.

segments.say: Every evening, the till at the Corner Cafe saves the day's sales as a file. On Friday, Asha adds four files up by hand. It takes an hour.
And the files are messy. One price is a word. One row has no price at all. One file is empty.

scenes.title: Plan it with AI
scenes.direction: Stage 1: the AI's plan, one big function inside except Exception. Asha checks it against Chapters 17 and 22 and asks for small parts.

messages.text: I am a beginner. I know files, CSV, JSON, try and except, functions and pytest. I want a weekly report from a folder of till CSV files with the columns item and amount. Some rows are damaged. Do not write code. Plan the functions, and say how to handle errors.

Write one function, `make_report()`, that reads every file, adds up the amounts and writes the report.
Put the whole body inside `try`, with `except Exception: print("Something went wrong")`, so it never crashes.

segments.say: In this project, all six AI stages help build one module: the report rules. Stage 1: plan. Asha asks for a plan, and says: no code yet.
The AI suggests one function that does everything, inside one big try, with except Exception. Its promise: it never crashes.
Asha checks it against Chapters 17 and 22. One big function cannot be tested in parts. And except Exception hides the real problem: the program never crashes, but it never says why.
So she asks for small functions with one job each, and a small try around the one line that can fail.

segments.say: Her six tests agree. The amount tests pass, and both week tests fail.

visual.heading: Asha's fix: the right key, the right exceptions
visual.hidden_text: The next screen counts the rows again.

segments.say: Asha fixes it with the rule from Chapter 22. Line 33: the right key, and her own parse amount.
Line 34 catches only the two exceptions she expects. Value error for the word four. And type error for the missing price, because float of None raises a type error.
Line 37 adds the sale only when nothing went wrong, in else.
Now Monday has four good rows. Tuesday and Wednesday each have one bad row. Thursday is empty.
And she runs all six tests again. Six passed.

segments.say: Step 5. Build week puts it all together. Line 48: glob finds every file ending in dot c s v. Glob gives no fixed order, so sorted puts them in name order.

visual.heading: The AI's test data crashes the report

segments.say: It crashes. A key error. Read the last line first: the key amount is missing.
Then the last file line shows where: line 33 of report tools, inside read sales. On your computer, these lines show the full path of each file.
Her except catches value error and type error, not key error. That is right: a whole file in the wrong format is not a damaged row.

visual.heading: Debug: the cause before the fix

messages.text: My report crashed with KeyError: 'amount' on a file you gave me. First explain the cause. Then show the smallest fix.

`DictReader` uses the first line as the keys, exactly as written. That file says `Amount`, so there is no key `amount`.
The fix: check the column names before the loop, and raise a `ValueError` with a clear message.

segments.say: Stage 5: debug. Asha pastes the error, and asks for the cause first, then the smallest fix.
The AI explains: Dict reader uses the first line as the keys, exactly as written. Its fix checks the column names before the loop.
Field names is the list of names from the first line. An empty file has none, so if columns lets Thursday through.

messages.text: All seven tests pass. Suggest one improvement that makes the report clearer. Do not change what the totals are.
Round each day's total to a whole number before you store it: `day_total = round(day_total)`. The report will show tidy amounts.

segments.say: Stage 6: improve. All seven tests pass. Asha asks for one improvement, and says: do not change what the totals are.
The AI says: round each day's total to a whole number before you store it. Tidy amounts.
Here is the AI's change, on line 56. Tuesday's real total is 11.25. Round with no second value gives the nearest whole number, as in Chapter 2.

ask.question: With the AI's line 56, what is Tuesday's total?

after.say: 11. And the week becomes 37 instead of 37.25. Asha runs her tests to be sure.

segments.say: Two tests fail: the week total, and the day that must not be rounded.
The suggestion broke her rule: it changed the totals. Rounding belongs in the display, and money already shows two decimal places. Asha keeps her version.
